correctness.rationale: For the original outside-neighbor fort definition, rim selection x_i=1 forces the corresponding leaf; at outside rim positions leaf membership is forced for exactly one selected cyclic neighbor, absent for zero neighbors and removable for two. Thus every minimal fort equals canonical B(X). Inclusion B(Y) subset B(X) for nonempty Y subset X is equivalent to equality of membership at the endpoints of each 101 pattern, i.e. Y is a union of components of H_X. Minimality is equivalent to H_X being connected; its connected support sets are parity-cycle intervals (n even) or bounded step-two intervals (n odd), giving the exact counts. Independently constructed graph adjacency and original fort predicate exhaust all nonempty sunlet subsets for 3<=n<=9 and match all predicted minimal sets; step-two support enumeration checks n<=18. A direct six-cycle subset check verifies the stated lifting obstruction.

value.rationale: The cited primary work raises the specific sunlet minimal-fort counting problem but gives only a lower bound. The exact structural classification closes it for all orders and reveals quadratic rather than purported exponential growth. The witnessed failure of a lifting principle is structurally meaningful for graph-corona operations and for selecting valid fort constraints in zero-forcing integer programming. This is not an arbitrary small graph count or a routine parity specialization: the infinite enumeration and explicit counterexample resolve a motivated discrepancy in primary literature.
